note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — FINE TUFT
tiles.details: Williamson County treatment: a many-stemmed fibrous-rooted bunchgrass with a shallow condensed branched rhizome; blades about 0.6–<2 mm in locally examined plants. Inspect PHOTO 1 for naturally growing fine blades and low clump; PHOTO 2 shows tangled dry and living leaves. The Bob Harms image (gallery panel 5) is a separate credited educational EXTERNAL habitat reference, not an excavated crown. The final CC0 garden photo documents cultivated habit only. None photographs a connected, exposed root/rhizome. New gallery panel 3 shows fresh blades and dead basal sheaths among moss and limestone; roots remain hidden.
tiles.short: Small tight perennial bunch with very fine often rolled blades
tiles.status: LIVE TUFT/HABIT PHOTOS; CONNECTED ROOTS/RHIZOME STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · EXPOSE THE REAL LIGULE
tiles.details: The Bob Harms Selected Central Texas Monocots MURE2-L photo (gallery panel 6) is a separate credited EXTERNAL educational reference that actually shows a sheath/blade junction with scale. It is not an archived CC-licensed image or an independently measured specimen; we have deliberately added no over-image arrow. Inspect a fresh same-plant sheath opened on its inner side with a 1-mm ruler. Published ligule reports conflict: local Williamson County <1–1.5 mm, minutely ciliate/splitting; wider GrassBase 2–4 mm or longer. Record which plant/shoot was measured. New gallery panel 4 shows ribbed outer tissue and dry sheath, NOT the free inner ligule.
tiles.short: Short membranous inner collar, often split; published lengths conflict
tiles.status: EXTERNAL COPYRIGHT-RETAINED LIGULE REFERENCE; SAME-PLANT LOCAL MACRO MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW THE OPEN PANICLE
tiles.details: Three locally archived exact-source wild flowering panels (Matt #58493566, Sam #4920088, Sam #5077102) show open fine branches, individual spikelet-bearing tips and hand context. These are ACTUAL seep flowering photos; don't confuse the immediately preceding MURE2-L photo with a panicle. Broad panicle color and one seedhead alone do not prove the ID.
tiles.short: Delicate widely branching head, not a dense Lindheimer plume
tiles.status: OPEN PANICLE PHOTO SUPPORTED; SCALE MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE THE TWO GLUMES
tiles.details: The Sam Kieschnick wild photo #5077102 (gallery panel 9) displays complete narrow spikelets, but not a disentangled pair of two glumes. Williamson County published specimen describes ~2.5–3.5 mm spikelet body excluding awn, two subequal one-veined glumes ~1.3–2.1 mm. These are published measurements NOT measured on the photograph; save microscopic dissection until a real local look-alike cannot be separated by habit, collar and full head.
tiles.short: Single-flowered spikelet ~2.5–3.5 mm; two shorter one-veined glumes

tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE LEMMA AWN
tiles.details: Local treatment: the single fertile lemma is about the length of the ~2.5–3.5-mm spikelet, with three veins and inward-rolled margins over the palea. Its fine terminal awn is described as <2–4 mm in local material; broader treatments may give different ranges. Two short palea tips must NOT be mistaken for separate long lemma awns. A whole spikelet photograph cannot prove lemma venation or the exact awn insertion.
tiles.short: One three-veined fertile lemma, slender terminal awn usually short

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Gallery panels 7–8 show genuine source-identified wild seep OPEN panicles; panel 10 is the clearly labeled DIFFERENT-SPECIES Lindheimer dense flowering head; panel 11 shows a second DIFFERENT-SPECIES coarse Lindheimer bunch. Panel 9 provides true seep solitary-spikelet context. Use whole-plant texture and branching head before dissections. Nimblewill's low rooting nodes and potential hybrid M. ×involuta remain separately provisional; avoid floral-color/cultivar guesses.
tiles.short: Lindheimer = coarser denser plume; nimblewill creeps; hybrid stays held
tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE LESSON; MATCHED DIAGNOSTIC PHOTO GAP

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: Find a fine, tight small bunch with threadlike sometimes involute blades. A true wild photographed OPEN branched panicle with tiny separate spikelets is now illustrated in three new source-licensed local images. Lindheimer has a larger fountain and a much more contracted densely packed head. Confirm by measuring a mature attached membranous ligule and spikelet; color alone and intermediate hybrid form are not proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Gallery panels 1–3: true source-determined seep fine leafy tufts; roots and a clean basal crown are HIDDEN. External Bob Harms natural clump (panel 5) and cultivated CC0 garden habit (panel 12) are context, not exposed-root photographs. New panel 4 shows dried OUTER sheath material, NOT opened true ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: The Bob Harms Selected Central Texas Monocots MURE2-L photo (gallery panel 6) is a separate credited EXTERNAL educational reference that actually shows a sheath/blade junction with scale. It is not an archived CC-licensed image or an independently measured specimen; we have deliberately added no over-image arrow. Inspect a fresh same-plant sheath opened on its inner side with a 1-mm ruler. Published ligule reports conflict: local Williamson County <1–1.5 mm, minutely ciliate/splitting; wider GrassBase 2–4 mm or longer. Record which plant/shoot was measured. New gallery panel 4 shows ribbed outer tissue and dry sheath, NOT the free inner ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Three locally archived exact-source wild flowering panels (Matt #58493566, Sam #4920088, Sam #5077102) show open fine branches, individual spikelet-bearing tips and hand context. These are ACTUAL seep flowering photos; don't confuse the immediately preceding MURE2-L photo with a panicle. Broad panicle color and one seedhead alone do not prove the ID.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Seep muhly tends to be a finer, smaller densely tufted perennial, with very thin often inward-rolled blades and a much more open wispy panicle than Lindheimer's stout large clump and contracted panicle. Its membranous ligule is generally shorter (GrassBase often 2–4[–9] mm versus Lindheimer often 8–15 mm); published local measurements differ, so use measured attached leaf parts plus one-flowered spikelets, never a hard ligule cutoff. Planted M. capillaris and its cultivars can show showier pink plumes but are not evidence of a local wild seep specimen. Parent-hybrid M. ×involuta requires actual hybrid-specific evidence.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: Find a fine, tight small bunch with threadlike sometimes involute blades. A true wild photographed OPEN branched panicle with tiny separate spikelets is now illustrated in three new source-licensed local images. Lindheimer has a larger fountain and a much more contracted densely packed head. Confirm by measuring a mature attached membranous ligule and spikelet; color alone and intermediate hybrid form are not proof.
memory_rule: SEEP: compact hair-fine bunch, built from condensed shallow underground rhizome branches + OPEN finely branched panicle with solitary small separated spikelets. Lindheimer: larger coarser bunch + comparatively dense narrow head. Root/rhizome close-up and true ligule still NEED PHOTOS.
safety_note: Status remains FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS, not FINISHED. Eight exact species images physically archived; Bob Harms source MURE2-a/MURE2-L references are REMOTE copyrighted educational images, and panel indices now match actual current canonical gallery. Do not imply measured inner ligule, excavated roots/rhizome or glume/lemma arrows where photographed pixels do not show them. Preserve all photo-level CC/NC rights, scientific holds and source determination.
field_rule: Start with an erect COMPACT basal tuft of extremely thin, often inward-rolled blades, generally smaller than Lindheimer muhly. At bloom, confirm the delicate OPEN branching panicle, often reddish, with one-flowered awned spikelets. Inspect the membranous ligule and the small leaf width on a fresh blade under magnification; color alone is not diagnostic.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
